q: Most facial muscles insert into:
explanation: Facial muscles typically insert into skin, allowing them to produce facial expressions.

q: Which muscle closes the eyelid?
explanation: Orbicularis oculi closes the eyelid.

q: Which muscle compresses the cheek, as when blowing air?
explanation: The buccinator compresses the cheek.

q: Which two muscles are the primary elevators of the mandible (jaw closers)?
explanation: Masseter and temporalis both elevate the mandible to close the jaw.

q: The masseter originates on the zygomatic arch and inserts on the:
options: Angle and ramus of the mandible
explanation: The masseter inserts on the angle and ramus of the mandible.

q: Contracting the SCM on one side only will:
options: Rotate the head to the same side
Rotate the head to the opposite side
explanation: Unilateral SCM contraction rotates the head to the opposite side while laterally flexing the neck.

q: Bilateral contraction of the SCM produces:
options: Neck flexion and assistance with forced inhalation
explanation: Bilaterally, SCM flexes the neck and assists forced inhalation.

q: The SCM originates from the sternum and:
explanation: SCM originates from the sternum (manubrium) and the medial third of the clavicle.

q: Bilateral contraction of splenius capitis produces:
explanation: Bilaterally, splenius capitis extends the head.

q: Which muscle raises the eyebrow?
explanation: The epicranius (frontal/occipital bellies) raises the eyebrow.

q: Which muscle raises the corner of the mouth, as in smiling?
explanation: Zygomaticus (major/minor) raises the corner of the mouth.

q: Scalene muscles, when contracting bilaterally during forced inhalation, primarily:
options: Elevate the first or second rib
explanation: Bilaterally, scalenes elevate the upper ribs to assist forced inhalation.

q: Which muscle depresses the mandible against resistance and tenses neck skin?
explanation: Platysma depresses the mandible against resistance and tenses the skin of the neck.

q: 'Mastication' refers to the action of:
explanation: Mastication means chewing.

q: Splenius cervicis originates from spinous processes T3–T6 and inserts on:
explanation: Splenius cervicis inserts on the transverse processes of C1–C3.

q: Which of the following muscles inserts on the orbicularis oris rather than directly on bone?
explanation: The buccinator inserts into the orbicularis oris, a soft-tissue insertion typical of facial muscles.

q: Temporalis originates from the temporal bone and inserts on the:
explanation: Temporalis inserts on the coronoid process of the mandible.

q: Unilateral contraction of splenius capitis produces:
options: Rotation and lateral flexion of the head toward the same side
explanation: Unilaterally, splenius capitis rotates and laterally flexes the head toward the same side.

q: Which muscle pair are synergists for closing the jaw, often both tense with jaw-clenching habits?
explanation: Masseter and temporalis work together to close the jaw and are commonly both tense with clenching.

q: The scalene muscles originate primarily from:
explanation: Scalenes originate from the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae and insert on the first or second rib.
